sections.title: One tool for each job
sections.content: You know this unit's three emphasis tools: cleft sentences (lesson 1), fronting (lesson 3) and contrastive *no ... sino* (lesson 4). When you write about a book or an author, give each tool its own job: a cleft sentence names the key idea, fronting stresses a quality at the high point, and *no ... sino* corrects an obvious first reading. Used well, they give a text rhythm.

sections.title: The tools in the text about Borges
rows: Lo que hace único este cuento es la idea del tiempo.
Insólita resulta la imagen de un laberinto hecho de tiempo.
No existe un único futuro, sino muchos futuros posibles.

items.spanish: Fue en 1941 cuando apareció el cuento por primera vez.
items.english: It was in 1941 that the story first appeared.

items.spanish: De esa imagen viene el título del cuento.
items.english: From that image comes the title of the story.

items.spanish: Lo que hace único este cuento no es la intriga, sino la idea del tiempo.
items.english: What makes this story unique is not the plot but the idea of time.

sections.content: Vary your sentences: alternate plain order (subject, verb, object) with a cleft or a fronted phrase. Two emphatic structures in a paragraph shape the reading; one in every sentence tires the reader.
